title: Day 5 Activity and Assignment
summary: Two therapists disagree over room preparation and shift responsibilities. Practise resolving the matter fairly, then write the steps you would take to resolve a disagreement with a colleague.

items.label: Focus
items.body: Fair conflict resolution: address the issue, disagree respectfully, stay private, escalate when needed, and restore professional cooperation

sections.title: Activity: Two therapists disagree over room preparation and shift responsibilities
paragraphs: Participants practise resolving the matter fairly.
Work in groups of three. One person is Therapist A, one is Therapist B, and one observes.
Use the same facts in every version. First, demonstrate an unconstructive version. Then replay the same situation fairly, using what you learned in Day 5.
The observer should note what changed. Do not name real colleagues.

sections.title: The situation
paragraphs: Therapist A finishes a session and believes room preparation belongs to the person starting the next appointment.
Therapist B is assigned the next client and finds used towels still in the room, the bed not reset, and shared supplies not replenished.
Both also disagree about who should complete the end-of-shift handover checklist.
The next client is due soon. A receptionist is nearby. Other staff can hear raised voices if the conversation stays at the door.

sections.title: Unconstructive version to demonstrate
paragraphs: Show how Day 5 problems look in practice. Choose at least three of the following.
list: Personal attacks: "You're lazy. You never do your share."
Treating disagreement as disrespect: "Who are you to tell me how to work?"
Gossip: telling other staff about the colleague instead of addressing the handover.
Taking sides: asking friends to support one therapist against the other.
Retaliation: refusing to pass on appointment information because of the disagreement.
Public argument in front of a waiting client or at reception.
Exaggeration: "You always leave everything for me."
Ignoring the operational problem while arguing about character.

sections.title: Fair resolution version
paragraphs: Replay the same situation. Protect the client's experience first, then resolve the disagreement privately and fairly.
list: Address the immediate operational issue: make the room ready for the waiting client.
Move the interpersonal discussion away from clients when it is safe to do so.
Use AGREE: acknowledge the other perspective, give yours respectfully, review facts, explore a practical solution, and establish the next step.
Use ISSUE: identify the actual problem, separate facts from assumptions, speak respectfully, understand the other perspective, and agree who will do what.
Challenge the idea or the process, not the person.
Do not gossip, take sides, or withhold necessary work cooperation.
If the two therapists cannot agree on whose duty it is, involve the supervisor with CLEAR facts rather than insults.
After the issue is addressed, continue professional communication even if they are not close friends.

sections.title: Facts the pair should clarify
list: What room-preparation tasks were incomplete?
Who was assigned the previous session and the next session?
What does the current handover or shift checklist actually require?
Was there a communication gap, or was an assigned duty left undone?
What must happen before the next client, and what should happen before the next shift?

sections.title: Observer questions
list: Was this disagreement or disrespect?
Did they address the room problem, or attack personality?
Was the conversation private enough for the situation?
Did anyone gossip, take sides, or retaliate?
When would supervisory help have been appropriate?
Did they agree on a practical next step, or only say "let's forget it"?

sections.title: Optional extra scenes
paragraphs: If time allows, replay one extra scene.

items.label: Scene A — Repeated incomplete handover
items.body: The same supplies problem has happened three times this week after a respectful reminder. Practise escalating to the supervisor with CLEAR, without rumours or public humiliation.

items.label: Scene B — After the apology
items.body: The issue has been clarified, but one therapist still refuses to share schedule updates. Practise MOVE: keep professional cooperation and raise exclusion if it continues.

sections.title: Assignment: Write the steps you would take to resolve a disagreement with a colleague
paragraphs: Write the steps you would take to resolve a disagreement with a colleague.
Use a realistic Zura Spa situation, such as room preparation, appointment changes, shared supplies, or shift responsibilities.
Do not name real colleagues in a way that spreads gossip. Describe roles and the work issue.
Be specific. "I would talk to her" is not enough. Show the order of your actions and which Day 5 habits you would use.

sections.title: How to complete the assignment
list: Describe the disagreement: what happened, who is affected, and what still needs to be done for the client or the shift.
Step 1: How would you protect privacy and dignity (and still fix any immediate service issue)?
Step 2: How would you address the issue instead of attacking personality?
Step 3: How would you disagree respectfully if you still see the situation differently?
Step 4: What facts would you check before assuming intention?
Step 5: What practical agreement would you propose?
Step 6: When would you involve a supervisor, and how would you report it professionally?
Step 7: After the issue is addressed, how would you keep professional cooperation without gossip, retaliation or taking sides?

sections.title: Example you may adapt
paragraphs: A colleague and I disagree about who should replenish towels after a session. I would first make the room ready for the next client. I would then speak privately: "The towels weren't replenished after the last session. Can we confirm whose checklist that is?" I would listen to her explanation, review the handover procedure, and agree who completes which tasks. If we still cannot agree, I would ask the supervisor to clarify responsibilities, using dates and facts, not insults. After that, I would continue sharing appointment information respectfully even if we are not close.

remember: Two therapists can disagree about room preparation and still resolve it fairly. Fix the operational problem, speak privately, focus on facts, seek help when the issue remains unresolved, and keep professional cooperation afterwards. Then write the steps you would take with a colleague.
